questions.q: What is the key difference between qc.rx(math.pi/4, 0) and qc.rx(theta, 0) where theta = Parameter('θ')?
options: There is no difference; both behave identically
The first bakes in a fixed numeric angle immediately; the second leaves the angle as a symbolic placeholder to be bound later
Parameter can only be used with the H gate
The second one runs faster on real hardware
questions.explain: A plain float angle is fixed the moment it's passed to rx(). A Parameter object is symbolic, turning the circuit into a reusable template whose angle is resolved later with assign_parameters.

options: A modified version of the original template circuit, which is no longer usable
A new, fully-specified circuit with theta bound to 1.57, leaving the original template unchanged
An error, since Parameter values cannot be reassigned
questions.explain: assign_parameters produces a new concrete circuit with the given value bound in. The original parameterized template is left untouched and can be bound again with different values.

questions.q: Using P(1) = sin^2(theta/2) for qc.rx(theta, 0) starting from |0>, what is P(1) at theta = pi (3.1416 rad)?
questions.explain: At theta=pi, sin^2(pi/2) = sin^2(90 degrees) = 1, so P(1) = 1.0 — RX(pi) is a full, certain bit-flip, just like the fixed X gate.

questions.q: At theta = pi/4 (0.7854 rad), what are the exact probabilities for qc.rx(theta, 0) starting from |0>?
questions.explain: Using P(1) = sin^2(theta/2) with theta=pi/4 gives P(1) = sin^2(pi/8) = 0.146447, and P(0) = 1 - 0.146447 = 0.853553.

questions.q: Why are Parameter-based circuits central to the variational algorithms covered in Chapter 6?
options: They run without any classical computer involved
They let an optimizer repeatedly bind new angle values, run the circuit, and score the result to search for an optimal angle
They remove the need for measurement entirely
They only work on real quantum hardware, never on simulators
questions.explain: Variational algorithms rely on a bind-run-score-repeat loop: a parameterized circuit template lets a classical optimizer try many angle values against the same circuit structure without rebuilding it each time.
